title: Order lifecycle and checkout flow
idea: The order lifecycle is a state machine: an Order starts PENDING_PAYMENT, moves only along allowed arrows, and every move tells Inventory what to do.
points: PENDING_PAYMENT moves to PAID on payment, or to CANCELLED on timeout or cancel.
PAID can ship or be cancelled; SHIPPED only becomes DELIVERED in v1.
Each move has a stock effect: commit, release, or restock with a refund.
An illegal move is refused in one place, not checked by every caller.

messages.label: checkout(cart C-1)
messages.note: The shopper presses Place order. The service reprices the cart first.

messages.label: reserveAll(lines)
messages.note: All lines are reserved together, or none are. Reserved units leave the available count.

messages.label: OR-1 PENDING_PAYMENT
messages.note: The order exists now, with frozen prices and a deadline to pay.

messages.label: pay(OR-1, token)
messages.note: Payment is a separate step; stock stays reserved while the shopper enters card details.

messages.label: charge(total)
messages.note: The service charges the frozen total, once, with the order's idempotency key.

messages.label: ok
messages.note: Payment succeeded, so the Order moves PENDING_PAYMENT to PAID.

messages.label: commit(OR-1)
messages.note: Reserved units become sold: on-hand and reserved both drop by the quantity.

messages.label: OR-1 PAID
messages.note: Had the deadline passed first, the sweeper would have cancelled and released the stock.

code.title: Status enum with effects
code.caption: Allowed moves live in the enum. Each accepted move updates one SKU's stock, so you can watch the counts.

walk.text: OR-1 is paid and shipped; cancelling after shipping is refused.
OR-2 is never paid, so it is cancelled; a late payment is refused.
OR-3 is paid and then cancelled by the shopper.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states; `canMoveTo` asks it.
Placing an order reserves its units straight away.
Refuse an illegal move and leave the status unchanged.
Pay commits stock; cancel releases it, or restocks and refunds if paid.

pitfalls: Do not set `status` from controllers or jobs; every change goes through `moveTo`.
A payment that lands after cancellation needs a refund, not a silent PAID.
Cancelling a PAID order must restock on-hand units, not reduce reserved ones.

quiz.q: What does the last line of OrderLifecycle print?
options: OR-3 PAID -> CANCELLED, onHand=1 reserved=2, refund
OR-3 PAID -> CANCELLED, onHand=3 reserved=0, refund
quiz.why: Paying OR-3 moved two units out of on-hand. Cancelling a PAID order puts them back, giving 3, and adds the refund note.

takeaway: Allowed moves live in one enum; each move carries its stock effect.

starters: Should there be a PAYMENT_FAILED state instead of staying PENDING_PAYMENT?
How would returns after delivery fit into this state machine?
Would the State pattern be better than an enum with a map?
